Individual fairness: a Lipschitz audit

Source: R/fairdf.R
lipaud.Rd

Dwork et al. (2012) ask that similar individuals be treated similarly: that the gap between two people's scores be at most lip times the distance between them, for a distance that says who is alike for the task. lipaud() checks the given pairs against that rule and reports the smallest constant the scores satisfy on them.

Usage

lipaud(h, d = NULL, pairs = NULL, lip = 1)

Arguments

h

The scores: finite numbers, one per person.

d

The distances: with pairs NULL, a stats::dist() object or a symmetric matrix between all the people (every pair is audited); with pairs, NULL (all 1) or one number from 0 per pair.

pairs

NULL, or the pairs to audit: a matrix of two columns of person numbers from 1.

lip

The constant: one number from 0.

Value

A list: lreq (the smallest constant the scores satisfy on these pairs), nviol and rate (the pairs breaking the rule at lip, and their share), ok (TRUE when none does), maxgap (the largest gap), worst (the first pair with the largest ratio), and pairs, a data frame with one row per pair: i, j, d, gap, ratio and viol.

Details

A pair at distance 0 is two people the distance cannot tell apart: any gap between their scores breaks the rule, and no constant repairs it (its ratio is Inf). The audit is only as good as the distance: it says whether the scores treat alike those the distance calls alike, not whether the distance is the right one.

References

Dwork, C., Hardt, M., Pitassi, T., Reingold, O. and Zemel, R. (2012). Fairness through awareness. Proceedings of the 3rd Innovations in Theoretical Computer Science Conference, 214-226. doi:10.1145/2090236.2090255

Examples

x <- c(1, 2, 2.5, 6)
h <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.60, 0.65)
# scores on a scale of 0 to 1 against distances in years
lipaud(h, dist(x), lip = 0.2)
#> $lreq
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $nviol
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 0.3333333
#> 
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $maxgap
#> [1] 0.55
#> 
#> $worst
#> [1] 2 3
#> 
#> $pairs
#>   i j   d  gap      ratio  viol
#> 1 1 2 1.0 0.10 0.10000000 FALSE
#> 2 1 3 1.5 0.50 0.33333333  TRUE
#> 3 1 4 5.0 0.55 0.11000000 FALSE
#> 4 2 3 0.5 0.40 0.80000000  TRUE
#> 5 2 4 4.0 0.45 0.11250000 FALSE
#> 6 3 4 3.5 0.05 0.01428571 FALSE
#>
